items.text: Pulse stores an emotional moment as a separate memory item, never as a field inside a decision.
Technical reports should use short conclusion headlines followed by one explanatory paragraph.
The installable Personal repository is pulse-personal; the Garden pulse directory is only the workspace entry point.
Pulse is atomic memory; Atlas owns the graph of people, projects, events, and relationships.
A Pulse release candidate cannot be published until the same archive passes installation on a separate physical Apple Silicon Mac.
Claude Mem remains disabled, but its database is retained as a migration source and must not be deleted.
A normal memory lookup should happen automatically without asking the person to type a recall command.
Project memories may surface only inside their verified Git repository; personal memories may cross projects.
When Pulse is unavailable, terminal, files, cancellation, and session completion must continue without a retry turn.
A useful memory answer should stay within 600 tokens in ordinary cases and omit weakly relevant material.
Cursor is outside the current release focus; the active product acceptance covers Codex and Claude Code.
The migration preview reported 68480 unique events, 5986 emotional marks, 55 capsules, and zero conflicts.
The active Personal database must never be rebuilt or migrated during benchmark runs; benchmarks use a temporary copy.
Benchmark quality is judged by correct final answers, not merely by whether a gold evidence row appears in retrieval.
Memory Home may prove that Pulse delivered context, but it cannot prove that the language model used that context.
